stage_a.note: Smiling and confident while explaining the product features.
High energy and excitement during the physical demonstration.
Friendly and approachable when handing out samples to the panel.

venture.description: Silicone rings designed as a safe alternative to metal wedding bands.
venture.note: Founders demonstrate the safety aspect of the rings using bodybuilders.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces himself to the panel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 introduces himself and states the ask of five hundred thousand dollars for seven point five percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks if they know what a standard ring is, calling it a finger amputation device.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains ring avulsion, noting it happens to many people and can severely damage the finger.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces the silicone rings as a safe alternative and brings out a professional bodybuilder.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 comments that the bodybuilder is a man.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 jokingly tells S3 to stay in her seat.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 notes the bodybuilder's pulling force is enough to tear a finger off.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 suggests showing what happens when a ring gets caught.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 commands the bodybuilder to pull, and the rubber hand rips.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 suggests trying again with a human hand and their silicone ring.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 brings out three more bodybuilders to increase the pulling power.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks S4 what she thinks of the bodybuilders.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counts down and they pull, causing the silicone ring to break safely.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses disbelief and asks to see the demonstration again.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 dismisses the bodybuilders so the panel can focus on the presentation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 tells the panel they brought samples for each of them.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains the curated selection of rings and invites the panel to try them on.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if the rings are all made of plastic.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 clarifies that the rings are made of silicone rubber.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks how many people wake up worrying about their fingers and how they acquire customers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits it is zero but emphasizes that it is a serious problem if it happens.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how they get anyone interested in understanding why they need the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that many people in the US have ring avulsion accidents every year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how many of those accidents result in ripped off fingers versus just pulled or strained.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 gives the example of Jimmy Fallon tripping in his kitchen and nearly tearing his finger off.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 adds that people with active lifestyles or specific professions constantly have to take their rings off.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks the founders to tell the panel about their background and how they started the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they have been friends their whole lives and started it after a rock climbing accident.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what they actually sell one ring for.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 states the retail price range for the rings.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what it costs them to make a ring.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides the manufacturing cost range for the rings.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 guesses that they have a ton of sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms they have done significant sales in the past eighteen months and projects more this year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses amazement at the sales figures.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks to confirm the cost of the cheapest ring.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms the cost.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the retail price of the largest men's ring.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 provides the retail price for that specific ring.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the manufacturing cost of that specific ring.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 provides the cost range for that ring.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks why that specific ring would cost four dollars to make.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains it contains actual gold flex to look like a real metal ring.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 expresses respect for their sales and says he is very impressed.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks where they are selling the rings.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that they sell entirely through their website and online marketplaces.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks to confirm that all sales are online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms and credits an amazing social media push.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what their sales were last month and how much they spent on marketing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shares their best month's sales and the average percentage spent on marketing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 notes they will spend over two million dollars in advertising and marketing.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 agrees with the projection.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 exits, stating they are a marketing company selling fear, which he does not see as a long-term business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters that while they started with fear, their largest market is now a jewelry trend.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 exits, citing familiarity with silicone products and too much competition in the market.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, feeling the messaging is mixed between safety and fashion, lacking clarity to hook customers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 notes that consumers sometimes create the message and praises their impressive sales despite confusing messaging.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 offers five hundred thousand dollars for twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 matches the offer of five hundred thousand dollars for twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S2 but indicates he cannot speak for his partner yet.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 calls them greedy but highlights the value of his platform and customer base.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 revises his offer to a loan with a per-order royalty until repaid, plus five percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 states he would consider a counteroffer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters S1, asking if he would be willing to do ten percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 declines but offers to split the difference at fifteen percent equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 advises the founders to take the money and run.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 tells the founders they are crazy to take the offer if they believe in their business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters S1 again, asking for twelve point five percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 refuses and sticks to his offer of fifteen percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks S1 and S2 if they have any interest in partnering together on a deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 declines the idea of partnering.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 also declines the idea of partnering.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 urges them to consider his loan offer, arguing it costs less if they are successful.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 argues his platform is valuable and his offer also costs less if they succeed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S2 but accepts S1's revised offer.

decisions.note: Believes it is a fear sale, not a long-term business.
Familiar with silicone and sees too much competition.
Finds the messaging mixed up between safety and fashion.
Impressed by sales and wants to leverage his platform.

decisions.terms: $500,000 as a loan, $2 per order until $1.5M, then 5% equity.
decisions.note: Offers an alternative structure to reduce equity.
Asks Robert if he would do 10%.
Tries to negotiate a slightly better equity share.
Accepts Robert's revised offer of $500k for 15%.

record.notes: Bodybuilders are present for the demonstration but do not speak.
